reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch treat Genesis 2 as narrating day six's chronological details rather than a competing order, posing no conflict with Genesis 1's joint creation.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen contrasts the Priestly account's simultaneous 'male and female' with the Yahwist's sequential man-then-woman order, of which this pairing is one instance.

quotes.text: In the one he sees astonishing mysteries in the difference of the sexes, in marriage, in child-birth (iv. 1); in the other these are physiological facts which raise no questions or reflections: "He made them male and female, and said, Be fruitful and multiply."
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), on the Priestly-versus-Yahwist treatment of the sexes in the two Genesis creation accounts.

sides.snippet: God created man in his own image. In God's image he created him; male and female he created them.
sides.verseText: God created man in his own image. In God's image he created him; male and female he created them.

sides.snippet: He made the rib, which Yahweh God had taken from the man, into a woman, and brought her to the man.
